title: Token backpressure playback - scratchpad
content:
Quick summary:
- After 2025-02-09 deploy (runtime v1.9.14 + batcher tuning) we saw sustained tokens/sec drop on a handful of production routes (english-generation: tokens/s from ~140k -> ~60k) while p50 latency improved slightly. Observed repeated oscillation: throughput drops, queue depth grows, backpressure logs spike, then recovery when autoscaler spins up extra capacity. Suspect interplay between token-based backpressure and continuous-batching window sizing.

Timeline (high level):
- 2025-02-09 03:15 UTC: deploy v1.9.14 (changes: batcher.window_ms default 50 -> 20, enable token_backpressure=true, rate_limiter refactor)
- 2025-02-09 03:40 UTC: first alerts (INF-4921) - p99 latency on route english-generation up to 800ms, tokens/s dropped on region-us-west-2
- 2025-02-09 04:05 UTC: scale-up, temporary recovery
- 2025-02-09 05:30 UTC: repeating oscillations every ~6-12 minutes

Commands and traces I ran locally (replay & quick repro):
- curl load pattern (50 concurrent clients, each sending ~200 tokens prompt):
  for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -X POST https://canary-infer.redwood.test/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","prompt":"lorem ipsum..."}' & done
- reproduction script produced same oscillation within 8m on canary host.

Collected logs (snippets):
- serving-runtime logs:
  [2025-02-09T03:46:12Z] batcher: window_fill_time_ms=52 batch_tokens=1024 batch_size=4 enqueue_delay_ms=12
  [2025-02-09T03:46:12Z] backpressure: token_bucket_drop=true tokens_dropped=230 refill_rate=10000 token_bucket_size=5000
  [2025-02-09T03:46:12Z] kvcache: hit_rate=0.12 eviction=LRU
  [2025-02-09T03:46:13Z] queue: depth=312 inflight=18
  [2025-02-09T03:46:13Z] scheduler: throttle_delay_ms=180 assigned_gpu=gpu-pool-a
- GPU side (nvidia-smi snapshots): GPU utilization ~35% during drop windows, memory stable.

Prometheus metrics (observed):
- tokens_served/sec (route english-generation): baseline 140k -> 60k after deploy
- batch_fill_time_ms P50/P95: baseline 18/42 -> 47/110
- queue_depth P95: baseline 12 -> 320 during incidents
- batch_size average: 6 -> 3 during drop windows

Quick hypotheses (ranked):
1) Token-based backpressure is too aggressive relative to incoming burst profile + smaller window_ms -> token bucket empties quickly, requests get dropped/requeued, leading to queue accumulation and oscillation. Evidence: token_bucket_drop=true logs correlate with throughput drops.
2) Batcher.window_ms reduction (50->20) reduced ability to coalesce tokens under bursty arrival; combined with token_backpressure triggers more frequent small batches -> worse throughput. Evidence: batch_size decreased from ~6 -> 3.
3) Rate limiter refactor changed refill semantics (now refill is smoothed) causing sustained low tokens/sec when many small bursts arrive vs previous instantaneous refill. Evidence: refill_rate=10000 looks same but effective refill timing changed in code path (see PR 1873).
4) KV-cache miss storm interacts: low hit rate (0.12) increases token generation per request, interacting with token bucket limits.

Commands/traces to instrument next:
- enable batcher debug flags for canary (export BATCHER_DEBUG_LOGS=1 on canary).
- add temporary metric: batch_fill_time_ms.sentinel and token_bucket_level gauge exported at 1s resolution.
- run synthetic burst test with controlled inter-arrival times: 200 QPS in bursts of 100 reqs/sec for 5s, then idle 10s. Observe batch_size distribution.
- try toggles: set token_backpressure=false on canary; set batcher.window_ms back to 50; set rate_limiter.refill_mode=instant (rollback refactor)

Temporary mitigation we tested (canary):
- token_backpressure=false + window_ms=50 -> tokens/s recovered to ~130k on canary, p99 latency stable, queue depth stayed <20. This is consistent with hypothesis #1/#2.

Planned experiments (small staged):
1) Short A/B canary across 2 hosts (one host baseline config, one host with minimal changes):
   - baseline: v1.9.13 (old rate limiter, token_backpressure=false, window_ms=50)
   - candidate: v1.9.14 + token_backpressure=false + window_ms=20 (isolates window_ms effect)
   - measure tokens/s, p95/p99 latency, batch_size distribution for 2 hours.
2) With token_backpressure=true, sweep window_ms in {10,20,50,100} and measure steady-state batch_size/throughput under representative mixed workload.
3) If refill_mode refactor suspected, put back instant refill for candidate and run same sweep.

Data to capture for each run:
- batch_size histogram (1s bins)
- batch_fill_time_ms (P50/P95/P99)
- token_bucket_level gauge (1s bins) and token_bucket_drop count
- queue_depth (1s bins)
- gpu_utilization (30s bins)

Notes / gotchas:
- Autoscaler masks some cases: when extra nodes come up throughput recovers, making root cause harder to reproduce at cluster-level. Use single-node canary to test purely scheduling/batching behavior.
- The request size distribution changed this week (we onboarded a partner sending longer prompts); need to ensure experiments reflect new token-per-request distribution.
- Prefill behavior: if prefill_enabled true and prefill is done on CPU before enqueuing, prefill latency skews batch_fill_time metrics. We should tag prefill vs normal requests in metrics.

Immediate next steps (today):
- (Arjun) enable BATCHER_DEBUG_LOGS on canary and collect 2h of traces (done, uploading to INF-4921)
- (Maya) run burst-sweep script against canary with token_backpressure toggled (scheduled 2025-02-12 16:00 UTC)
- (Jun) add temporary token_bucket_level gauge to exporter and open quick PR to push to canary (PR draft linked above)

Longer-term possibilities:
- Consider adaptive token bucket sizing based on observed moving-average request token consumption (instead of fixed bucket/refill)
- Add heuristics: if batch_size drops below threshold for >N windows, temporarily relax token backpressure for the route for T seconds
- Move refill semantics to a hybrid instant+smooth model for burst absorption

Questions to resolve / open items:
- Was the rate_limiter refactor intentionally changing refill semantics? (Ping @infra-rl on PR 1873 for design notes)
- Should token_backpressure be on by default for dedicated customers? We saw a measurable cost/latency tradeoff.
- How to classify prefill vs real-time requests in metrics without heavy code churn? Quick idea: add header X-Request-Phase: prefill|live and propagate.

Raw grep commands used: 
- kubectl logs -n serving runtime-abc -c runtime | grep backpressure | sed -n '1,200p' > backpressure-snips.txt
- prometheus query examples:
  max_over_time(sum by(route) (tokens_served_total{route="english-generation"}[5m]))
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(batch_fill_time_ms_bucket[1m])) by (le))

Attachment pointers:
- uploaded traces: gs://redwood-dbg/token-backpressure/2025-02-09-traces.tar.gz (linked in INF-4921)
- canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serving/canary-batcher?orgId=1&var-host=canary-01

If/when we revert token_backpressure across prod clusters we should monitor cost impact (more tokens served -> higher bill). Keep finance/telemetry in loop before wide rollback.

Scratch TODOs (one-liners):
- add batcher debug flag to helm chart (temp)
- create short-run canary job with fixed tokens-per-request distribution
- verify kv-cache hit-rate won't change across experiments (control variable)
- write short postmortem once root cause confirmed

End of scratchpad.

---- notes to self: keep this file lightweight. Move finalized notes to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/incidents/ when done.
